exposure: New Japanese diagnostic criteria (final version) for obstetrical DIC (assesses main underlying disease, fibrinogen level, and fibrin/fibrinogen degradation products or D-dimer level)
Previous Japanese diagnostic criteria for obstetrical DIC (assesses underlying disease, clinical symptoms, and various laboratory findings)
outcome: Diagnosis of obstetrical disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
Scores >= 8 according to the previous Japanese criteria
cohort: The study analyzed 212 women with singleton pregnancies who delivered after 22 gestational weeks and experienced blood loss >= 1000 mL during vaginal delivery or >= 2000 mL during cesarean section, excluding those with missing laboratory findings before receiving blood transfusion at delivery.
finding: The new Japanese criteria (final version) for obstetrical DIC demonstrated effectiveness, reliability, and validity, showing significantly higher frequencies of fibrinogen levels < 150 mg/dL and scores >= 8 by previous criteria in the obstetrical DIC group, with good Cronbach alpha and Spearman's rank-order correlation between the new and previous criteria.
